title: Circus
text: “Waah……”

Kuro-chan slipped quietly between Father and me, as if trying to hide. Come to think of it, most Filolial-sama seemed to dislike monster merchants' tents. Amid that, Kuro-chan had gone in without a care… but now, had she finally gotten scared? Now that I thought about it, Black Thunder too had been full of bluster at first when talking with Ark, only to suddenly put some distance between them. Perhaps Kuro-chan was the same sort—someone who charges in without really understanding the situation, then senses the danger and decides to back off? Her sense of danger might just be a bit slower than other Filolial-sama, I say. Filolial-sama of the Aria species, like Sakura-chan, tended to be gentle and easygoing types, after all. Black Thunder and Kuro-chan probably had that same gentle streak in them too.
“Now then, this is the slave our shop recommends.”
What was introduced was a wolf man, indeed.
“Grrrrrr… Gaah!”
Clang! The wolf man, radiating raw ferocity, let out a roar from within his cage, baring his fangs at us in threat.
“Hmm……”
Father glared at the wolf man without so much as flinching.
“Is this what a Melromarc slave is like……?”

Siltvelt's envoy kept tilting his head in confusion, again and again. Father shot him an irritated look, as if to say, “What's the matter?” Since this was all an act, he didn't say anything outright, but Siltvelt's envoy seemed to catch on and nodded.
“No… it must just be my imagination.”
“As for what kind of country Melromarc is, Hero-sama… I imagine you've heard from your companion.”
“Ah… yes, I've heard about that. This is a place that deals in demi-humans and beastmen, isn't it?”
“That is correct, yes. And as for the slaves……”
The monster merchant activated the slave crest.
“Gaaaah! Kyain, kyain!”
The slave crest on the wolf man's chest lit up, sending him writhing across the floor. That settled him right down.
“So it was the slave crest.”
“Ah, you already knew of it?”
“I've heard a great deal.”
“Well then, that makes things quicker. Yes.”
“How much for this one?”
“Well, seeing as this breed excels in combat… shall we say seventy-five gold coins, as a special discount?”
Seventy-five gold coins as a discount? That was quite the steep price. Still, it wasn't out of reach.
“I see. Let me have a look at the other slaves as well.”
“This way, please.”
With that, they made a full round of the slaves the merchant had on offer.
“Hmm… so this is about the range, is it.”
“So then, is there any slave here that catches Hero-sama's eye? Yes.”
“May I ask you something?”
“What might that be?”
“I'm thinking of starting a business using slaves. Do you have any good ideas?”
So he was asking the merchant directly—first inquiring about the merchandise, and now this.
“Oh my? You, Hero-sama? Yes?”
“Something wrong with that? I got set up by this country too. In a world like this, I ought to be allowed to do as I please, shouldn't I?”
Father answered while fixing the merchant with a chillingly murky stare. At that look, the merchant's expression grew faintly rapturous.
“Oh, Hero-sama. Those eyes of yours—you seem to possess a truly splendid disposition.”
“Answer the question.”

“Of course. Well, first, buying slaves and forcing them into various forms of manual labor is a common approach. From farming to anything else requiring manpower, they can be put to use for it all. In the past, some have even been made to row at the bottom of ships. Yes.”
The merchant added that forcibly clearing wastelands was another common use.
“Having them dig in mines would also be recommended, I'd say.”
“Hmm… that sort of thing, is it.”
“Then there's also… running a circus caravan that doubles as a means of acquisition. Yes.”
“Oh? A circus, is it.”

“Yes. Putting rare demi-humans and beastmen on display, performing acrobatics to provide entertainment across the land, while behind the scenes buying up unwanted mouths to feed and selling them off elsewhere—that's the standard method of acquisition.”
“Sounds like it could easily be used for kidnapping too.”

“How rude! I take great pride in my business. I may deceive customers with falsehoods now and then, but I never lie about my merchandise. Kidnapping and plunder are the work of third-rate scoundrels! Yes!”
Father's face took on a look of faint exasperation.
“……Certainly, it's true that because of the Waves, there are some deplorable people out there committing such savagery. Yes.”
Even so, the merchant's response on this point felt a bit weak.
“By the way, when it comes to acquiring humans in Melromarc, it's handled as being sent off into service. Yes.”
“So no slave crest is carved into them, but their family is saddled with debt to keep them bound—something like that?”
“That is correct, yes. Depending on the circumstances, they may end up being sold as slaves in other countries.”
I see—so that was how they got around the problem that humans couldn't be made into slaves. As ever, their cunning knew no bounds, I say.
“Hmm… a circus, is it.”
“Are you interested?”

“The people of this country made a spectacle of me and reveled in it, so it shouldn't be so bad if I get to enjoy myself in turn, should it? Tormenting savage beasts and bending them to my will—don't you think that's truly wonderful? Especially that wolf man just now… the way he writhed about from the slave crest was thoroughly amusing.”

Father let out a low, performative chuckle—kukuku. After all, Father was the sort who found things unpleasant except when watching someone he disliked suffer. Even then, he only enjoyed an enemy's suffering for a little while before his brow would furrow with unease—so deep down, his heart was a kind one, indeed. As for me, though, I could enjoy watching Crimson Swine and Takt suffer no matter how much or how long it went on. I could hardly wait to start making them suffer. So I too let out a wicked laugh from behind them.
“Hero-sama, both of you……”
“Hmm?”

Siltvelt's envoy took a step back, at a loss for words, while Kuro-chan looked back and forth between Father and me, tilting her head in confusion. So Father leaned in and whispered something to Siltvelt's envoy. At that, the envoy nodded repeatedly in understanding and put on a matching villainous smirk.
“Still, even if you're putting on a circus, you'll need some kind of centerpiece attraction. Even if we were to lend you our merchandise……”
“I already have something in mind for that. Kuro, show us your true form for a moment.”
“Hm? You want to see Kuro's true form, Dark Lightning?”
“Yes. Reveal your true self, Jet-Black Fang and Claw, and strike fear into their hearts right here!”
“Waah! Got it!”
Since Father played along, Kuro-chan enthusiastically transformed into her Filolial form. With a poof, into her Filolial shape, I say.
“Ohh!”

“There's a trick like this up my sleeve. Naturally, I have various other methods too. More than anything, training demi-humans and beastmen to perform tricks for show—wouldn't that go over well in Melromarc? For that matter, wouldn't the sight of me whipping the slaves into submission be a hit too?”

Oh? Father, doing the whipping? Since Father couldn't attack, it wouldn't hurt or itch in the slightest. No, in fact—since it didn't hurt or itch at all, he could keep whipping away forever. That meant he could satisfy the sadistic urges of Melromarc's nobility indefinitely. All an act, of course. The sight of Shield Hero, the very god of demi-humans and beastmen, whipping demi-humans and beastmen… surely even the people of Melromarc couldn't complain about that.

“The initial funds, of course, I'll secure myself. You'll provide a reasonable number of slaves I deem suitable, and I'll travel around buying and collecting slaves while running the circus. How does that sound?”
“Splendid! Indeed, with that approach, there's certainly a good chance of success. Yes! Please, allow me to cooperate with you by all means. Yes!”
The monster merchant began rubbing his hands together. He'd clearly spotted the potential for profit.
“So teach me the ropes, at least to some extent. The methods related to slaves too.”
“Understood! Yes!”

And so it seemed Father ended up learning all sorts of things from the monster merchant. Since Father seemed to be telling us to go do as we pleased while he talked business, I ended up leaving the tent together with Siltvelt's envoy and Kuro-chan. But along the way, I… stopped by the egg lottery corner. And sure enough, just as expected, the pattern on an egg lit up.
